Pele Yoetz, Introduction 1: Pele Yoetz (Wondrous Counselor), Mighty God - has wondrously shown His kindness and truth to all His creatures without limit and without number. Who can express the mighty deeds of the LORD, who can proclaim all His praise? It has no end and cannot be completed, and silence is His praise. And above all these good things is this: that He chose Israel as a treasured people, gave them Torah and mitzvot, and called them the portion of His inheritance. And His hand is still outstretched to do further good to His people, doubled good. He is the One who feeds and sustains, and His hand is open to every living soul for sustenance and provision. He is the Healer of all flesh, who wondrously performs rescue and removes every illness. He gives life to all the living, in kindness and compassion, and His kindness is better than life, for He helps His people Israel with Torah and service - this is a greater good than all the life of the World to Come. And if I said, let me recount how His kindness has overwhelmed me, I would not know how to tell it, and there are no words - I am too small for all the kindnesses and all the truth that the awesome-in-deed God has done, with the disgrace of a person like myself, a trivial creature. I shall bless the LORD who has counseled me, and who has helped me until now shall help me further, for the sake of the honor of His Name, forever. And my soul has longed and even pined to merit the many, to please and give satisfaction to my Creator, my Former, and my Maker, and God was with me; may the name of the LORD be blessed and exalted above all blessing and praise. And already, in the past, my hand produced, with the help of God who dwells on high, a pamphlet, "Orot Elim," from the collected words of our holy Rabbis, words of the living God - fitting words to adorn the bride [Torah]. Happy is the man who listens to the words of the wise, which are like goads guiding a person on the paved way of life. And now I have come, in a scroll-book written concerning myself, my offspring, and the people of my generation, to speak good counsel, according to the smallness of my own vessel and according to what my hand has attained to learn and to teach from the mouths of books - which is the straight way a person should choose to do what is proper and right in the eyes of God and man - favor, favor to it. And I have gathered it in sayings, pure statements of God, in a brief manner, in alphabetical order, for the sake of the unification of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, and to adorn the bride. And so, by the leave of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, I have named this book "Pele Yoetz" [Wondrous Counselor], for in the word PELE is hinted my own lowly name, among the thousands of Eliezer Papo, may his end be good - I am a counselor to myself and to the people of my generation, a treasured people. And further, my hands have also prepared, with the help of Shaddai, [another work called] "Also the sparrow has found a home, a house of prayer" - an awakening concerning prayer, and an order of prayers and supplications for every man according to his occupation and for every trouble that should not come - great is prayer, if he does not fulfill it entirely. Let not the crushed one turn back ashamed, but find sufficient redemption. And how much more so when they plead in prayer for the sake of the honor of Heaven - God shall hear from heaven, and revive him within two days. Truly they said (Berachot 32b): great is the power of prayer - set your heart to its strength, for we have nothing to rely on but the mercy of Heaven, who hears the voice of supplication, the voice of prayer.
Pele Yoetz, Introduction 2: And so I have lifted my eyes to heaven: I, [before] the merciful Father God, who does righteousness with all flesh and spirit, grant me that my words be remembered and acted upon, and that they bear fruit for Your service and for satisfaction before the throne of Your glory, and that I too be built up and merit to repair my own faults and complete the repair of nefesh, ru'ach, and neshamah, and that I rejoice in the offspring of my loins when I see them doing Your will as You will, and that I never be ashamed, nor consumed, nor stumble forever. Please, LORD, save now! Please, LORD, prosper now all Your people Israel, and among them myself, the least, a trivial creature.
Pele Yoetz, Introduction 3: And to you, people, I call out: my brothers and my people, take this Torah book, and in this and through this, learn well, for your own good. Listen, and your soul shall live; you shall attain gladness and joy in this world and in the World to Come, one gladness after another. Be strong, and let us strengthen ourselves for our God; let us have pity on the honor of our Maker, who, because of our sins, stands in the midst of the exile. Come, let us return to the LORD; let us serve Him with gladness and joy, like the joy of a bridegroom over a bride, to arouse love and to join the beloved ones together in gladness. Perhaps God shall take counsel and hasten the redemption for us. So may it be His will, speedily in our days, Amen.
Pele Yoetz, Introduction 4: And behold, they said in Midrash Rabbah, Parashat Acharei (22:2): if a person has no mitzvah established for generations, what benefit does he have? And therefore I have chosen this mitzvah, to merit the many. And I have already stated this in the pamphlet "Orot Elim," in Tractate Shekalim (page 28), that I cast my supplication before the LORD: please, LORD, deal with Your servant according to Your kindness, and let me dwell in His tent forever. And I also entreat all who know the [religious] law, that they read in my book and expound my words to the many, in synagogues and study houses - perhaps God shall take counsel for me and grant me that my words bear fruit, and thus my soul shall rejoice in it. And if I merit to behold the pleasantness of the LORD and to visit His Temple, I shall repay well whoever brings me any benefit - my fellow, storekeeper for storekeeper. And especially concerning the offspring of my loins, my seed and my seed's seed forever, an obligation is placed upon them to cherish my words and to strive with even greater effort to expound them to the many, and to greatly guard, perform, and fulfill everything found written in my pamphlet, for the honor of their Creator and the honor of their parent.
Pele Yoetz, Introduction 5: And truly shall my palate utter, for I recognize my own low worth, the least of all worths, that I am not fit to give rebuke, and am not worthy that people should benefit from me with counsel and wisdom - and how much more so, for I fear the mockery of the complacent, and I worry lest, God forbid, guilt roll about through me, as I have written within, under the entry "Espah" [gathering] - see there. But this was my first thought: that my soul thirsted, longed, and even pined to fulfill what is written (Genesis 18:19), "that he shall command his children and his household after him, and they shall keep the way of the LORD" - as I have written under the entry "Tzava'ah" [testament] - see there. And therefore I did this, and took the trouble to have it printed with the help of Heaven, so that it endure many days for my seed and my seed's seed forever - and perhaps God shall favor me and grant me that my pamphlet also find favor in the eyes of others, the people of my generation, and they shall learn from it and expound it to the many, and shall do me a kindness - as I have written under the entry "Tochachah" [rebuke], at its end - see there. And it is easy for the understanding one to know that there are matters not fitting to expound before the multitude of the people, and likewise there are words fitting to skip over out of concern for the honor of the listeners, such as not to mention "am ha'aretz" [an ignorant person] and the like - and I have already marked with a half-moon sign like this ( ) in a place where it is fitting for the expounder before the many to skip - and from the places I have marked, the wise shall hear and add insight for the other places I have not marked, and for other books. Every prudent person shall act with knowledge according to the place, the time, and the need of the hour. There is a place where they said to elaborate, and there is a place where they said to be brief. And how good and how pleasant it is, when one comes to expound before the many, whether orally or from the book, that he first arrange the sermon two or three times to himself, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, taught - even if he knows of himself that the LORD has graced him with an eloquent tongue, it is a mitzvah to listen to the words of the wise, and he shall find benefit for himself, that he clarify his own words, refinement after refinement, until "the knowledge of his lips speaks clearly" and "the words of a wise man's mouth are gracious."
Pele Yoetz, Introduction 6: And before I finish speaking, behold, my lips shall not withhold from thanking the LORD, who does good with His creatures through His agents, men of kindness. May the LORD do good to the good ones, those who volunteer among the people, who did me kindness with their bodies and their money, and were a help to me from the city, and came to the help of the LORD among the mighty. Happy are those who keep justice, who do righteousness at all times - these men are complete, both the one who gives much and the one who gives little - and since they are many, I shall not lift up their names upon my lips. Behold, I have taken up a simple, ordinary blessing as it is, and I am a prayer: please, LORD, look down from Your holy dwelling, from heaven, and bless Your people Israel. May the LORD repay those who do good, they and their children and their households - may they attain gladness and joy, may they eat the fruit of their deeds, with the good increasing in this world, doubled good in healthy children and long life and wealth and riches in their house; may there be peace within their walls, tranquility within their palaces, and may the principal remain for the World to Come, and their righteousness stand forever. And my brother Yaakov, may he live long, may he too grow great, may he see enduring offspring, may he live long days, and may the desire of the LORD prosper in his hand - Amen, so may it be His will.
Pele Yoetz, Introduction 7: And now let the power of the LORD be great, the right hand of the LORD is exalted, the right hand of the LORD performs valiantly - arouse Your might and come to our salvation, gather our scattered ones and bring us up with joy to our land, and let the Temple sit upon its rightful place as before, for the honor of the Shechinah. May He who redeemed the fathers redeem the children, if not by merit, then by mercy. These are the words of a mortal, a man of little worth, diminished from vanity, who writes and signs in the city of Silistra, may it be protected, at the end of the month of Nissan I give [this work], in the year "happy are those who sow beside all waters" [i.e. the year 584] (=5584). May the LORD see and greatly turn back His anger.
Pele Yoetz, Introduction 8: The lowly one, Eliezer, son of the honorable Rabbi Yitzchak Papo, may his end be good.
Pele Yoetz 1:1: Love of the Holy One, Blessed Be He - There is no attribute better than love of the Holy One, blessed be He, for from it flows all the service of the Name, blessed be He, and all unity. And one who serves out of love is not comparable to one who serves out of fear. And the Rabbi, author of "Sefer HaBrit," has already gone deep, expanded, and elaborated at length in explaining the root of love and fear, with good sense and knowledge - "the words of a wise man's mouth are gracious" (Ecclesiastes 10:12). Happy is the person who is diligent in his own words. And for the sake of the task before me, I shall come briefly and write a few notes for myself and for the people of my generation, according to what I have learned from the words of the aforementioned book and other books that my eyes have seen, to serve as a reminder before my eyes - and may the LORD God help me for the sake of the honor of His Name.
Pele Yoetz 1:2: Now, love of the Holy One, blessed be He, is one of the 613 commandments, and it is a constant mitzvah, which is in a person's power to fulfill at every time and every moment through remembrance, and it is fulfilled through thought and reflection alone - for when he takes to heart that it is fitting to love the LORD with intense love, he thereby fulfills a great mitzvah. Now, these mitzvot that are fulfilled through thought alone are easy to fulfill, since a person cannot exist without thought even for a moment - and if he thinks strange thoughts and evil imaginings instead of thinking of love of God, blessed be He, and His fear, and the like, this is nothing but an evil heart, forsaking the fountain of living waters to hew broken cisterns (Jeremiah 2:13) - and in a place where he could perform a mitzvah and receive reward for it, fools passed by and were punished. And therefore it is fitting for a person to strengthen himself with great might and force to distance all strange thoughts and evil imaginings, and to think holy thoughts even while going about his business, and as soon as he remembers that he is not doing well, that he is thinking strange thoughts, he shall be distressed and flee and cling to his Maker as much as he can.
Pele Yoetz 1:3: Now, there are two kinds of love: one is love because of what one receives - for he shall take to heart that it is the way of a man to love someone from whom he sees benefit, even a small benefit, and all the more so if it is a great benefit, and all the more so if he gives him his whole livelihood and enough for his need and repays him with good kindnesses - he shall surely say, how shall I repay this man, who has done me kindness and a free gift? Even if I lived a thousand years, I could not repay him thanks; if he sends me to distant places in the middle of the night, I am obligated to obey him, I cannot turn him away empty-handed, for I owe him much. And if his fellow saved him from some illness or great pain, or from some heavy defect or loss of a limb, his love toward him shall grow, and if he saved him from death to life, his love shall grow even more and more. And so on and so forth - there are several levels of love, each higher than the last - and all the more so, doubled and redoubled love is fitting to have for the Creator, since all the good things in the world, whether they come by the hand of Heaven or by the hand of man, all of them are from Him, blessed be He, for it is He who places in the heart of His creatures to do good to one another, and He has many agents, the Omnipresent.
Pele Yoetz 1:4: And if many evils and troubles passed over his head, and he was saved from them, he is obligated to love the God who redeems and saves and answers and has mercy at every time of trouble and distress - and all the more so, and an a fortiori argument, if the Holy One, blessed be He, did him kindness such that his own eye never saw evil, and he was saved from the evils prepared to come upon him and stirring to come into the world - so that it is found that His kindness, blessed be He, overwhelmed him - and of this they said (Devarim Rabbah 2:37): "let every soul praise the LORD" - that for every single breath he is obligated to give praise. And let Israel now say, with what shall we approach the LORD, let us bow before the God of the heights (Micah 6:6), who has repaid us with good things beyond measure and beyond number, and while we stand and provoke Him, He has not dealt with us according to our sins nor repaid us according to our iniquities. And let him not let slip from his thought the formula we say in the praise of "Nishmat Kol Chai": "and were our mouths full of song as the sea," and so on, "in famine You sustained us, and in plenty You provided for us, from the sword You saved us," and so on - and let him reckon, in fine detail, how many good things He has done him from the day he was in his mother's womb, and from how many evils He saved him, both those revealed to him and those hidden from him, along the lines of what they said (Niddah 31a; Pesikta Zutarta, Chukat 21:9): the one for whom a miracle is done does not recognize his own miracle - whether they came upon him and he was saved, or whether they were prepared and did not come upon him - for all of this a person is obligated to take it to heart and love his Creator with intense love.
Pele Yoetz 1:5: And all these good things are vanity compared to the good of the soul, which is truly a great good, beyond comparison. Of this let Israel rejoice in its Maker, who chose us from among all the peoples, and gave us a Torah of truth, and planted eternal life within us, and sanctified us with His commandments, and chose us to serve Him and to bless in His Name - through which we shall merit, live, and inherit good and blessing for the life of the World to Come, which is a great good, so much so that they said (Avot 4:17): better one hour of tranquility of spirit in the World to Come than all the life of this world. And this is considered while he is serving in order to receive reward, but when he reaches the level of being like servants who serve their master not in order to receive reward (Avot 1:3), then he shall rejoice more and more that he has merited to be a servant to an exalted and lofty King, awesome and fearsome, whose greatness is unfathomable, who chose us from among all the peoples and from all the heavenly host, and desired us and loves us - and the Holy One, blessed be He, wished to give merit to Israel, therefore He gave them abundant Torah and mitzvot, and desires our love though we are man, likened to vanity - this is a good beyond compare for whoever contemplates deeply the greatness of the Creator, and, corresponding to it, the lowliness of man. Through this he shall recognize and know that it is a great good that He chose us and drew us near to His service, to the point that they truly said (ibid. 4:17): better one hour of Torah and good deeds in this world than all the life of the World to Come. And let him imagine in his mind what honor and greatness is bestowed upon a lowly man, whom the king desires to honor and chooses to stand before him and serve him, even though he is flesh and blood, a putrid drop like himself - all the more so, how many good levels the Omnipresent has bestowed upon us, to a place our own hand cannot fully reach, so great are the good things our Creator, our Former, and our Maker has bestowed upon us.
Pele Yoetz 1:6: And in truth, what there is to rejoice over concerning the good things of this world and the rescues from evils is that through life and goodness we can reach the great good, which is to serve our Creator. And this is the evil of death and of harm, that they prevent us from serving our Creator - for otherwise, this and that are one and the same, since his days are like a passing shadow, and the evils and the goods of this world are vanity, vanity of vanities, all is vanity - only that we desire life and goodness insofar as it seems to us that they assist us in the service of the Name, blessed be His Name. And this is the intent of what we say in the praise of "Nishmat Kol Chai," after we say "and were our mouths full of song as the sea," and so on: "until now Your mercies have helped us" - meaning: this is our joy over all the good things and the rescue from evils, that Your mercies have helped us toward Your service.
Pele Yoetz 1:7: Behold, it is so: each and every person, according to how the Holy One, blessed be He, has helped him in his service, is so obligated to love his Creator for the abundance of good. For the good that all of Israel has in general, that He gave us a Torah of truth, good statutes and mitzvot, is not comparable to the good bestowed upon one to whom He gave strength, health, and sufficient ability, and settledness, quiet, and tranquility for the service of the Name, blessed be His Name. And whoever has made his portion among those who sit in the study house has received a greater good than others. And whoever the LORD has graced with wisdom and knowledge to conduct himself with good attributes and uprightness, and to recognize the disgrace of forbidden things and bad attributes and to distance himself from them, in a manner that he finds favor and good sense in the eyes of God and man by doing what is upright and good - this is a great, abundant, and precious good beyond measure. For all this, a person is obligated to love his Creator with intense love according to the abundance of the good, and submit greatly before Him, and say (Genesis 32:11), "I am too small for all the kindnesses and all the truth that You have done Your servant." With what shall I approach the LORD and repay Him thanks? And so on and so forth, the living person shall take to heart, and shall go deep and expand in his thought with pure thoughts, until his heart is kindled with the sparks of the flame of love of the Creator. And more shall be written of this, with the help of the Name, under the entry "Simchah" [joy] - see there, for love and joy are one and the same thing.
Pele Yoetz 1:8: And there is another kind of love that comes from the side of the intellect, and it is called "the love of exaltedness." For whoever has good intellect, who recognizes the merit of the perfect man, and whose heart desires perfection, loves the perfect man for his perfection with intense love - and all the more so should one love the Creator, blessed be He, who is the true perfect One in every kind of perfection, to the ultimate degree of perfection. But this love is possible only among those who resemble each other, one who desires good and walks in the way of the good - and therefore, the more a person increases his occupation with Torah and fulfills His commandments, blessed be He, since He, blessed be He, fulfills them because the precepts of the LORD are upright, and walks in His ways, blessed be He, so his love toward Him for His perfection shall increase - and whenever his hands grow slack from Torah and from mitzvot, so he shall retreat from love of the Creator, whether because he then has no resemblance to the Creator, or further because his sins are the curtains separating between him and his Father in Heaven, and they are the accusers and adversaries that confuse his mind with many thoughts until he does not remember, or cannot persist in his thought, in love of his Creator.
Pele Yoetz 1:9: And since we are orphans of orphans, greatly impoverished, and our impurity and guilt have increased, and our sins withhold the good from us, and we are unable to direct our minds to fear and love the glorious and awesome LORD - behold, it is thus good for a man to set fixed times to read, every single day, or at least occasionally, in books that mention fear and love and the like, such as the holy book "Reshit Chokhmah," the book of the pious author, the Shelah, the book "Chovot HaLevavot," the book "HaBrit," and the like. And through these words of ours, perhaps there is hope to fulfill in part the mitzvot "to fear and to love," for fear is drawn from love - for according to the abundance of love, whether because of the good things received from Him or because of His exaltedness and perfection, so he shall fear to transgress His will and to anger and grieve Him. Also, the mitzvah of fear is fulfilled through thought alone, as shall be written below under the entry "Yera'eh" [fear] - and from the thought of love, the thought of fear shall be drawn along with it.
Pele Yoetz 1:10: And a person can arouse love and fear from any physical thing and the like - for example, if he eats or drinks something pleasant to his palate, or delights his soul's richness with excursions and hearing a pleasant voice, marital relations, and earning money that accrues from them, and the like - he shall take to heart: if I love this thing so much, which ceases and is lost, vain and empty, which was here one night and gone the next night, how much more so should I love the Creator, who is the source of all loves and pleasures, and from whom flow the wellsprings of life and all pleasures. And he shall banish his mind from love of the physical thing and cling to love of his Maker, and let the servant say (Exodus 21:5), "I love my master!" (Song of Songs 7:7), "how beautiful and how pleasant is love among delights!" And likewise, when he fears and is afraid of some cause among the causes of the events of the times, he shall take to heart and say: why should I fear this thing, which is likened to vanity - it would be better for me to fear God instead. And he shall immediately exchange it and turn the evil into good, and receive a fine reward, and find sufficient redemption for himself.
Pele Yoetz 1:11: And just as we have said that the attainment of love and fear all depends on the abundance of deeds and on the abundance of study in Torah and in books of ethics, so, according to the abundance of love and fear, love of Torah and mitzvot shall increase. For love is recognized in doing the will of one's beloved with all one's heart, all one's soul, and all one's might - "many waters cannot extinguish love" (Song of Songs 8:7). And according to the abundance of his love, he troubles himself even with great effort, and shall consider it as though bearing a heavy burden for many days, and they shall seem to him like a few days, in his love for his Creator, just as one does for love of money and other loves. And it suffices for a person that he love Torah and mitzvot as he loves money, his wife, his children, and the like - would that it be so, even [only] like a priestess as like an innkeeper's wife [i.e., even a lesser degree would be welcome]! And by this a person shall know whether he has reached the level of one who loves his Creator: when he shall rejoice at His word like one who finds great spoil (Psalms 119:162), and shall be more careful about the loss of time - even a moment - without occupying himself in Torah and mitzvot as much as he can, more than he is careful about the loss of ancient wealth, for it is more precious than pearls, and all that you could desire cannot compare with it (Proverbs 3:15). And truly they said (Avot 6:2): woe to people for the disgrace of the Torah! For there is no greater disgrace than for one who could earn great spiritual gain and give satisfaction to his Maker, yet does not care. And if he occupies himself with jest and idle talk, of him Scripture says (Jeremiah 2:13), "they have forsaken Me, the fountain of living waters, to hew for themselves broken cisterns." Happy is the person who listens to reckon the reward of a mitzvah, that he gives satisfaction to my Maker through it, for better one hour of Torah and good deeds in this world than all the life of the World to Come. And it is all the more necessary to be diligent in a place where there is a loss of money, that he not love money more than love of the Creator. And whoever abandons the service of his Creator, from occupying himself with Torah or with any mitzvah that comes to his hand, because of some matter, it follows that he loves that thing more than the Creator, and it is worthy of disgrace and wrath. And in whatever he occupies himself with matters of this world, he shall consider that the purpose of his occupation with that matter is so that it be a help for the service of God, blessed be His Name, and all his deeds shall be for the sake of Heaven, along the lines of the verse (Proverbs 3:6), "in all your ways know Him, and He shall straighten your paths." This is a great principle in the Torah, for through this he shall not go out of line, and he shall weigh all his deeds in a balance, by measure and weight and measure, and it shall follow that all his days are only occupied with the Torah.
Pele Yoetz 1:12: And there are many kinds of loves that are incumbent upon a person, and all of them are drawn from love of the Creator. This one comes out first. And after it:
Pele Yoetz 2:1: Love of Oneself - It is a nature that the Creator has implanted in man, that he love himself, and a man is close to himself and loves himself more than the whole world and more than anything in the world, for all that a man has he shall give for his own life. But there is a bad evil - the evil of the evil inclination, which seizes the corners of the eyes and makes a person like one sick or drunk, who does not know his right from his left, and causes evil to himself, consuming himself from soul to flesh, in a manner that no enemy in the world could harm him as much as he harms himself - and this is great folly. And truly they said (Sotah 3a): a person does not sin unless a spirit of folly enters him. For whoever is a fool, sometimes his folly shall lead him to destroy himself knowingly, God forbid. And whoever has a brain in his skull shall take to heart that it is fitting for a person to love himself, his body and his soul, that a good reward be gathered for him in his labor, that his soul delight in richness, and even his flesh shall dwell securely.
Pele Yoetz 2:2: And according to upright reason it is fitting for a person to love his body more than his money, and "better a dry morsel in tranquility and rest than precious wealth with much toil" (Proverbs 17:1). And if the LORD has widened his boundary, let him give his money a means of providing relief for his body, and not toil in this world over the gain of money, unless he has [enough] to do good to his body, and shall be a merciful man to his own soul - provided he not be among wine-guzzlers, meat-gluttons, eaters of delicacies, who increase excursions day and night, who increase marital relations like roosters - for all these consume from soul to flesh, as shall be further explained in its place. And above all, guarding against anger is necessary, for they said (Ecclesiastes 11:10), "remove anger from your heart and put away evil from your flesh."
Pele Yoetz 2:3: And whoever is not careful of anything harmful to his body, it follows that he is his own enemy, seeking his own harm, and shall be destined to give an accounting - for if one who injures others has a transgression on his hands, all the more so one who injures himself, and is a cruel person to his own flesh. And all the more so must he guard himself in a place where there is even a doubt of doubt concerning danger to life, and if he brings himself into a place of danger for the benefit of money, it follows that his money is more precious to him than his own life, and if a miracle is done for him, they deduct from his merits - it follows that he sells his merits and the abundant good treasured for him for the World to Come, the reward of mitzvot, for any amount of money, which ceases and is lost, and moreover he shall be punished - and he deserves to be liable with his own life for having transgressed the word of the Merciful One, who warned: "take heed to yourself and guard your soul greatly" (Deuteronomy 4:9), "and you shall greatly guard your souls" (ibid. 4:15). Therefore a person shall not stand in a place of danger, such as on dangerous roads, or by way of seas and rivers, unless he is under absolute necessity for the sake of his livelihood, and he shall take with him nourishing men to accompany him, in order to lessen the danger by natural means. And if he can go by dry land, he shall not go by way of seas and rivers, which are more dangerous. And according to the degree of danger, so, if a miracle is done for him, they deduct from his merits. Therefore, whatever he can do to lessen the danger through money or extra effort, he is diligent and rewarded, and the merit exceeds the expense, and the mitzvah "and you shall greatly guard yourselves" which he fulfills is worthy that it protect him, save him from all trouble, and leave a blessing in his house, and he shall be whole in his body and whole in his money (and more shall be written of this below, under the entry "Shemirah" [guarding]).
Pele Yoetz 2:4: And the essential love, that he love himself, his body, and his soul, must be drawn from love of his Creator - just as a person loves his own household utensils and is careful with them, that they not become soiled or broken, because he loves himself and wishes to make use of them, so he shall be careful with his body and his soul, even more and more, that they not become soiled or broken, since they are the ministering vessels with which to serve before the LORD, the Master. And this shall be his entire intent in guarding his body and his soul, and he shall conduct his affairs with judgment, and the LORD shall be his help and be his strength.
Pele Yoetz 3:1: Love of Sons and Daughters - Love of sons and daughters is also required by nature, since they are bone of his bones and flesh of his flesh, and even a raven desires its young. But one must be careful that love not corrupt the proper order, that one not discipline his son and give him too much affection and excessive love - and Solomon already said in his wisdom (Proverbs 13:24), "he who withholds his rod hates his son, but he who loves him disciplines him diligently." And the essential love is love of the soul, and included in this is love of oneself, for a son gives merit to a father, and it is written (ibid. 29:17), "discipline your son, and he shall give you rest, and give delights to your soul." Therefore a person shall be careful to conduct himself with his children with open rebuke rather than hidden love, all according to what the son is: in his youth, "folly is bound in the heart of a child; the rod of discipline shall drive it far from him" (ibid. 22:15) - but the father shall be careful not to be cruel to his son and strike him in his anger with a fresh, cruel blow, but rather guide him calmly and strike him mercifully on the legs, not in a place where he could cause a defect, such as between the eyes. And when he is older, "a rebuke [enters more deeply] into a person of understanding" (ibid. 17:10). And it is known (Mo'ed Katan 17a) that whoever strikes his grown son transgresses "before the blind," and so on - and not literally a full-grown adult, but rather according to what the son is and according to his own character. And when he is even older, so that he does not accept a rebuke, "a gentle tongue breaks a bone" (ibid. 25:15). And he shall not disgrace his honor before others, so as not to make his own reputation foul. And it is even more necessary to be careful of what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, warned us (Shabbat 10b), not to distinguish between one son and the others, for jealousy is as harsh as Sheol (Song of Songs 8:6). The principle is: according to the son's own mind and character, the father must conduct himself with him in a manner that he not sin - and if he does sin against him, let him hasten to forgive him, so that his son not be punished because of him, and let him not be so exacting with them - and sometimes he shall make himself as though deaf, not hearing, and as though not seeing, and sometimes he shall set aside his own will for theirs. And this is a great principle for one who wishes to merit his own soul and the soul of his children after him.
Pele Yoetz 3:2: And the essential thing, to give satisfaction before our Father in Heaven, is that he strive with all his might and strength to teach his children Torah. And how good is his portion and how pleasant is his lot if his children are Torah scholars! Let the man rejoice in the offspring of his loins, in this world and in the World to Come. And at the very least, let him devote himself to strive with all his soul and all his might that his children not be ignorant of Torah, for great is the evil of the ignorant, without understanding. For there is a way that seems straight to a man, but its end is the ways of death. And an ignorant man cannot be pious (Avot 2:5). And if he cannot merit for all his children the crown of Torah, at least let him have one son among his sons who is a Torah scholar, whose Torah is his profession. And let him pour out his soul before the LORD that his children be masters of Torah, complete in attributes and in opinions. And let him also fast at times over this, so that his sins not withhold the good from his children. And especially must a person keep his eyes open concerning his daughters, for a person does not know what shall be their lot - therefore he shall be careful to distance them from all bad attributes, and teach them all kinds of women's work, and accustom them to minimize sleep and to all good attributes, and counsel them with good counsel on how to conduct themselves with their husband in the straight and good way, in a manner that she find favor and good sense in the eyes of God and in the eyes of her husband.
Pele Yoetz 3:3: And every prudent person shall act with knowledge, and his eyes shall observe his children's thoughts and their schemes, and he shall use his strength to distance his son from being a man skilled in hunting [i.e., deceit]. And a speaker of falsehood he shall distance, for truth is the foundation of the structure. And he shall strive to distance his son from vulgar speech and from uttering an oath, and likewise distance him from every trace of prohibition and from ugliness and the like - and especially from the sins of youth, extra guarding, knowledge, care, and diligence are needed. And let him not trust in his children and rely on saying, my son shall not go down into the counsel of the wicked, and shall not stand in the way of sinners - for there is no guardian against forbidden relations (Ketubot 13b, Chullin 11b). And whoever is greater than his fellow, his inclination is greater than his (Sukkah 52a), and much it causes [ill]. And bad companions do much harm (Mishnah, Sotah 7:1). Therefore let him gird his strength to distance his children from bad company, as much as comes to his hand, and strive with all his might that they walk in the way of the good and keep the paths of the righteous (Proverbs 2:20). This is the essential great pain of raising children, and reward is according to the pain (Avot). Let him rejoice in the offspring of his loins in this world, and let his soul rejoice for the World to Come.
Pele Yoetz 3:4: And this love too must be drawn from love of the Omnipresent, that he strive to gather many workers for the Omnipresent - for this is the whole fruit of sons and daughters, that they do the will of their Maker; otherwise they are "children in whom there is no faithfulness" (Deuteronomy 32:20), and the absence [of such children] is better than the presence of evil. Therefore this shall be his entire aim in loving his children, to fulfill his Creator's commandment, to give satisfaction to his Former.
Pele Yoetz 4:1: Love of Man and Wife - Love of man and wife is an obligatory matter, that there be intense love between them. And let us begin with a husband's love for his wife, for the saying of our Sages, of blessed memory, is known (Yevamot 62b), that he is obligated to love her as his own body and to honor her more than his own body. However, he shall not, in his love for her, be withheld from the service of the Name, blessed be He. And the Tanna has already warned (Avot 1:5), do not engage in much conversation with a woman - concerning his own wife they said that whoever engages in much conversation with a woman causes evil to himself and becomes idle from words of Torah, and in the end inherits Gehinnom. And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Bava Metzia 59a): whoever follows his wife's counsel falls into Gehinnom. Therefore every prudent person shall act with knowledge, and as they said (Sanhedrin 107b), that the left hand should push away and the right hand draw near. And the essential love is love of the soul, and it is incumbent upon him to rebuke her with pleasant speech, and to guide her in the ways of modesty, and to distance her from slander and anger and curses and mentioning the Name in vain, and the like - the Order of Nashim [women's laws] and the Order of Nezikin [torts, i.e. avoiding harm] - and to warn her of the details of the mitzvot, especially all the prayers and the blessings over enjoyment and the observance of the Sabbath and the like. And how good and pleasant it is to teach her words of ethics and tell her the words of our Sages, of blessed memory, in all matters relevant to her, and the severity within them, for then her heart shall tremble and she shall be more careful than the man.
Pele Yoetz 4:2: Now, there is no need to speak to one to whom the LORD has given a prudent wife and who has found a good wife, for certainly a thread of kindness is drawn upon her and she is beloved by her husband. However, especially careful must be the man upon whom an evil fate has fallen, a difficult wife - he stands in a great trial and must strongly conduct himself with her in peace and companionship, for the honor of the Shechinah, for these are ancient matters. And he shall take to heart that "the flame fell among the cedars" (Mo'ed Katan 25b), to the point that they said (Yevamot 63a): his judgment is that "lighter" ones [women] save us from sin - and they, our own men, said: a woman's hair is long and her understanding is short - therefore the intellect must come from him. And if she oversteps his judgment and angers him, he shall guard his spirit lest he become angry at her, and needless to say, not disgrace her, curse her, or strike her - heaven forbid - for this is the custom of boors, worthless, and reckless people, and he injures his own soul - rather, with soft speech and a sweet palate he shall rebuke her, and in any case he shall endure and be insulted rather than insult, and accept the judgment of Heaven with joy, for "from the LORD is a wife for a man." And according to the saying of our Rabbis, of blessed memory (Eruvin 41b), who said that whoever has a bad wife does not see Gehinnom - it would be fitting to seek a bad wife, if one could withstand the trial, given the severity of the judgment of Gehinnom - and since he withstands the trial, he shall not inherit two Gehinnoms, but rather shall accept it with love and receive a fine reward for his labor.
Pele Yoetz 4:3: And he must also strengthen himself to arouse love, so that his children not be, God forbid, children of a hated wife, and reward is according to the pain (Avot). And the fence to prevent quarrelsome words from his house is not to be so exacting about household expenses over every single penny, for "a woman's jealousy of her fellow wife is as harsh as Sheol." Therefore, a man of means shall increase his household's honor, a thing in its proper time, and shall appease his wife, for blessing does not rest within his house except for the sake of his wife (Bava Metzia 59a), and great is peace in the home, to the point that they permitted erasing the great Name to bring peace between a man and his wife (Nedarim 66b). Therefore, let a man use his strength to remove evil from his house and cause the Shechinah to dwell in his house.
Pele Yoetz 4:4: And included in this love is that he not go far away on a long journey for a long period of time, for besides that he causes harm to himself, as we shall explain under the entry "Machshavah" [thought], with the help of Heaven, there is also within it physical pain for his wife, for "love is as strong as death" (Song of Songs 8:6), and when her husband is separated from her she is a poor, suffering woman, living a life of pain. And at the very least he shall be careful to appease her with words, with a letter of greetings, to mix the blood of love, and according to what his hand attains, a man shall send from time to time gifts and objects, to revive the heart of the downtrodden and gladden his wife's soul and dispel her sorrow - and it shall be counted as a great mitzvah, whether little or much.
Pele Yoetz 4:5: And even greater shall be the obligation upon the wife to love her husband and honor him like a king among his troops, and to fear him, and to fulfill his desire and his will with all her strength, and her whole aim and mind should be to strive to fathom her husband's mind and know what he desires, and to do his will as his will, so that she find favor in his eyes. And the essential love, which is love of the soul, [means] she shall devote her soul to help him in the service of the Name, blessed be His Name, for this is her portion. And with the sweetness of her lips she shall speak to him if she needs to guide him in a good way, and comfort him in his time of trouble. And she shall rise while it is still night to encourage him and serve, together with him, one shoulder, in the service of the Name, blessed be His Name - and needless to say that she shall be careful with all her might not to be a cause of harm, that he become idle from the service of the Name, blessed be His Name, because of her, God forbid, for that woman shall bear her own iniquity. What shall I say - not all minds are equal, but everything is according to what kind of man he is; she must conduct herself with him according to his own character, with grace and good sense, so that their match rise up well in love and brotherhood. "The wisdom of women builds her house" (Proverbs 14:1), and "a woman who fears the LORD, she shall be praised" (ibid. 31:30). For besides needing to be modest - "all the glory of the king's daughter is within" (Psalms 45:14) - so that she not cause men to sin through sight and approach, she must also be adorned for her husband and careful about cleanliness and purity and in the order of expenditure, so that her husband not sin by setting his eyes on another - and these deeds of hers shall also draw her closer and cause her to find favor in her husband's eyes.
Pele Yoetz 4:6: Now, a woman given into the bosom of a God-fearing man, and how much more if she finds him a man of Torah and greatness, shall certainly, obviously, honor him and love him with intense love. However, it is even more necessary to urge a woman upon whom has fallen the lot of a man harsh in his attributes and his opinions, despised and lacking in stature, devoid of all good - not for this reason shall she make light of his honor in her eyes and despise him in her heart, God forbid, but rather in any case she shall be careful of his honor, whether he is good or a sinner, whether lowly or honored, for the matter of the King, the King of the universe, rests upon her, and what has she to do with the secrets of the Merciful One, for God settles the solitary and He mixes matches - therefore, whatever is incumbent upon her to do, she shall do. To what is this comparable? To a man whom the king desires to honor and has made viceroy to the king, whom all the people are obligated to treat with honor even if he is a leper or has a discharge - so is this matter. And just as the woman is careful with the mitzvah of niddah, challah, and the kindling of the lamp, so shall she be careful with her husband's honor, for so the King has commanded her, and her reward shall be great as her deeds prove that she does these things for the sake of their purpose and fulfills the decree of the King of the universe. And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Tanna DeVei Eliyahu Rabbah 9): there is no fit woman among women except one who does her husband's will. And let all women take instruction from the story brought in the Talmud (Nedarim 66b) concerning Bava ben Buta, about that woman who gave honor to her husband, and struck Bava ben Buta on the head because she did her husband's will. Therefore let all women give honor to their husbands, from great to small (Esther 1:20).
Pele Yoetz 4:7: And there are women lacking in knowledge, who make strife with their husbands over household needs that he does not provide, and this is great folly. Whichever way you look at it: if the husband is poor and unable to provide, his own distress, hardship, shame, and humiliation are sufficient for him, since he is ashamed to reveal to his wife that he cannot afford it. And the wife must have good sense and not add distress to his distress, but on the contrary, comfort him with the pleasant speech of her lips and say to him: do not be distressed over the lack of money, for the LORD shall never forsake us, and days shall come when there is plenty, when we shall have our fill of bread and be well off, or there shall be the satisfaction that our table shall be full of richness for the World to Come, for not every person merits two tables, and this world is vanity and emptiness. Let my father arise, eat your bread with joy, for man lives even by bread alone. And she shall speak such good words to him with grace and kindness, until he is joyful and gives thanks for his portion, a good fate that has fallen to his lot.
Pele Yoetz 4:8: And if the LORD has widened her husband's boundary, and nevertheless he is stingy with household needs or delays bringing them for some reason - what does it matter to her? Whatever he has brought, she shall set before him, and he shall eat. Could he say to her, why have you not made me delicacies as I love? She shall say to him, from where should I make what you have not brought? And if she makes strife over clothing, jewelry, and human pleasures, this too is vanity and vexation of spirit, for "better a dry morsel with tranquility in it" (Proverbs 17:1). And if the great Name, written in holiness, is permitted to be erased for the sake of peace in the home (Nedarim 66b), all the more so must husband and wife forgive and set aside their own will for the sake of peace in the home. And the wife must be concerned that perhaps her husband is not as well-off as she thinks, and does not wish to tell her that he cannot afford it, thinking that this would worsen her fortune [in her eyes], and the like - sufficient claims he may have for not fulfilling her wish. Therefore she shall not press the moment nor override his judgment to increase expenditure against his will, without his benefit. And likewise the wife must be concerned, when her husband is angry at her over nothing, that perhaps he had some trouble in the marketplace, and out of the abundance of his talk and anger he has spoken until now - as people say: whether he could or could not [succeed in the marketplace], he quarrels with his wife [either way]. And she must endure, and not anger him further nor cause him further pain.
Pele Yoetz 4:9: And this is a great principle: if there is a quarrel between people, or between a man and his wife, and one of them "let out the water, the beginning of strife" (Proverbs 17:14), and went out of line and opened his mouth without restraint - the other party shall use his strength not to respond to him with anything, good or bad, at the time of his anger, but rather wait until the wrath passes, and after a day or two has passed, then he shall rebuke him to his face, peacefully, evenly, and with gentle language, and say to him: why did you do so? What is my transgression, what is my sin, that you pursued me and were angry with me, anger without violence in my hands? Was it good in the eyes of the LORD? And similar good words. Whoever does this loves peace and pursues peace, and there shall be peace within his walls, tranquility within his palaces. These are the sustainers of the world, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Chullin 89a) on the verse (Job 26:7), "He hangs the earth upon nothing [belimah]" - that the world endures through whoever restrains [bolem] his mouth at a time of quarrel, for through this the dispute remains essential [i.e., contained] and does not beget [further strife].
Pele Yoetz 4:10: And a woman upon whom has fallen the lot of an evil, worthless man, who strikes and curses, tramples and violates - she shall accept upon herself the judgment of Heaven, and shall endure and not weary of atoning for her soul, for her reward is good for the World to Come. And a woman of valor, a prudent woman, shall not reveal her husband's disgrace and his bad temperament and nature to creatures, and her voice shall not be heard, so that her husband not be disgraced and not come to hate her further for having revealed his disgrace - for then his anger shall smoke, and his wrath shall burn within him, and he shall strike her further, a greater blow for these. And all the more so she shall not reveal to her father, mother, or brothers anything of her own evil situation, hardship, and pain - for what benefit is it to her that her father, mother, and brothers suffer distress of soul, and moreover that a fire burn within them over their daughter's trouble, and they go forth to meet with weapons and make strife with her husband until the flame of the dispute rises - and that woman shall bear her own iniquity, and eat the fruits in this world, that she become hated by her husband and he treat her worse for having revealed matters between him and her.
Pele Yoetz 4:11: And therefore, her father, mother, and relatives, if they have knowledge and understanding within them, even if they are told of the daughter's evil situation, that it is grave, shall act as though they knew nothing at all, and receive her husband with a pleasant countenance for the good of their daughter. And even if they wish to raise their voice and rebuke him to his face, they shall seek a way to show as though the matter had been heard from the neighbors, who heard through the window, and the like. And it is best that it not be revealed at all, as we have said, so as not to distress them and so that they not hate him in their hearts - but rather she shall be like a bride found complete in her father-in-law's house and pursued to go and tell her praises in her father's house, and she shall tell them that everything is good for her in her home - and it shall be counted as a mitzvah for her that she gladden the heart of her father, mother, and relatives, and she is worthy that it be a shield to grant her a good end. And it is even better that she herself rebuke him at an opportune time, with pleasant speech, with grace and kindness - certainly this shall bear more fruit, for truly they said (Proverbs 25:15), "a gentle tongue breaks a bone." And she shall also pour out her soul before the LORD day by day - perhaps the LORD shall favor her and her prayer shall bear fruit to bring her husband back to a good path, and she too shall find rest.
Pele Yoetz 4:12: And included in a wife's love for her husband is that she pray for him before the LORD, for a woman's prayer, since her heart is soft and her tears are readily available, if she cries out to the LORD from the depths of her heart, her prayer shall certainly bear fruit. And likewise the wife must pray for her children, for in the peace of her husband and her children shall she have peace, and who shall have more compassion for them than she? (And if God is with me and I arrange a pamphlet, "Seder Nashim" [Order of Women], as is in my heart, I shall also write prayers relevant to women, with the help of Heaven.) In accordance with this, the wife shall be careful and take care not to bring a lawsuit against her husband [before Heaven] and not to shed tears over him - for although it is more incumbent upon him to be careful, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Bava Metzia 59a): a person must always be careful about wronging his wife, since her tears are readily available, her wronging is quick to bring punishment upon whoever wrongs her and causes her pain - nevertheless she too shall take to heart that if evil comes upon her husband, God forbid, she takes the first share of it, and it is her own soul that is injured. And let all the people hear and fear from the story brought in the Talmud (Ketubot 62b) about the wife of a certain Rav, who was waiting for her husband to return from the road, and afterward he did not come, and she shed two tears over him out of her distress, and immediately her husband died at her hand - even though he had done her no evil and had not intended to cause her pain. And it seems that there is a moment of His wrath that causes a person to die for a light cause, God have mercy. Therefore let children tremble not to cause their wives pain, and let trembling seize the wives, not to shed a tear over their husbands, but rather to seek mercy for them. These are some of the ways of uprightness for a man and wife who have been blessed - let the wise hear and add learning. And there is already, in the book "Shevet Musar" by our teacher Rabbi Eliyahu HaKohen, of blessed memory, chapter 1, in the order of conduct of husband and wife - see there - and so may they do, and so may they continue to conduct themselves with one another in a good way according to their own characters, so that the Shechinah dwell between them, there being peace in their tents.
